entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 52_Europa_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 3666 vertices and 7328 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 319 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (255°, 40°), period 5.629954 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 159.12972831753473 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: The live source folder https://observations.lam.fr/astero/Data/52Europa/ contains Deconv/ and Red/. Reduced and deconvolved observations therefore have a concrete archive route. Their pixels, image geometry, coverage and photometry were not qualified in this directory-level check, so these files cannot yet be treated as a registered global reflectance map. The current grid remains an explicit missing-imagery presentation.
entries.revisitWhen: The original image headers and publication establish a usable projection onto this specific MPCD model, and a native-pixel comparison qualifies geometry, illumination and measured coverage.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 52_Europa_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation or scientific comparison specifically requires this alternative mesh and its matching source frame.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 65 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 1072 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.10 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.65; 1 of 65 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. A photograph lens for this body would rest on the survey's record read by the route proven on Vesta and on five elongated bodies, with no check on this body itself; it is not derived until one exists. The outline does not place it either: 52 of 65 frames score, but they leave 6.213 degrees after a 5.070-degree floor, twice the three-degree gate. Measured outside preparation by the registration stage's own limb rule driven from the pinned inputs, which reproduces Sylvia's prepared report to the digit; the stage's own number can differ, and on Themis it read 1.65 degrees where this route read 2.92.
entries.revisitWhen: A registration reference for this body: a spacecraft map, or frames in which the cross-frame test resolves markings (peak correlation above 0.15 with a mirror margin above 1.5 on most frames).
